attrs.title: Signs your feed is holding you back
attrs.lead: In Shopping ads and free listings, your feed decides which searches you show for and how your products look. These are the problems we see most.

items.title: Hundreds of products are disapproved or limited
items.text:
Merchant Center lists the errors, but not always clearly. A missing field, a policy problem or an image issue can each block hundreds of products, and every one of them is a product that can’t show in Shopping ads or free listings.

We group the errors by cause, fix each one at the source, in your store, a feed rule or a supplemental feed, and request reviews where needed. Then we check the diagnostics every week so new errors don’t pile up.

items.title: Titles are copied from your store
items.text:
Store titles are written for people already on your site: short, branded, sometimes just a product name. In Shopping, Google matches searches to the title, so a product called “Aurora” never shows for “brass pendant light 40cm”.

We rewrite titles with the words people search: brand, product type, key attributes such as size, colour and material, and the model. We do it with feed rules for large ranges and by hand for best-sellers.

items.title: GTINs, brands or sizes are missing
items.text:
GTINs (barcodes), brands and model numbers help Google match your product to searches and to other sellers. Without them, products are often limited, and clothing, shoes and furniture need sizes, colours and gender too.

We add identifiers from your suppliers’ data, mark your own-brand products correctly, and fill in the attributes each category needs. Limited products become approved.

items.title: Shipping, tax or returns are rejected
items.text:
Merchant Center needs shipping costs, delivery times and, in some countries, tax and return settings. If they’re missing or don’t match your site, products can’t show in that country at all.

We set shipping, delivery times, tax and returns for each country you sell to, so they match what customers see at checkout. Products then show everywhere you deliver.

items.title: Prices or stock don’t match the site
items.text:
When a sale starts, a product sells out or a price changes, the feed has to change too. If it doesn’t, Google flags a mismatch, and repeated mismatches can lead to a warning or a suspension.

We set the feed to update on a schedule that matches your store, handle sale prices properly and add structured data to your product pages so Google reads the right price.

items.title: You haven’t set it up yet
items.text:
Many stores never set up Merchant Center, or set it up years ago and forgot it. That means no Shopping ads, no free listings and none of the product searches where people are ready to buy.

We create and verify the account, connect your store, set up shipping and tax, and build a clean feed. Free listings go live first, so you get product traffic before you spend anything on ads.

attrs.label: How we set it up
attrs.html:
How we set it up

From an empty or broken account to an approved feed in one to two weeks. You see the changes before they go live.

  1. We look at your store, your product data and any existing Merchant Center account. We list every error and warning, group them by cause and check your shipping, returns and policies against Google’s rules.

    You get: An audit with what to fix first.

    • Store platform and product data checked
    • Errors and warnings grouped by cause
    • Shipping, returns and policies reviewed
    • Best-sellers and margins noted

  2. We create or clean up the account, verify and claim your website, and add business details, shipping, delivery times, tax and returns for every country you sell to.

    You get: An account Google can approve.

    • Website verified and claimed
    • Business details and contact information
    • Shipping and delivery times per country
    • Tax and return settings

  3. We connect your store, then improve the data: titles, descriptions, identifiers, categories, images and custom labels. Feed rules cover large ranges; best-sellers get written by hand.

    You get: A feed ready for review.

    • Store connection or feed file
    • Titles and descriptions rewritten
    • GTINs, brands and attributes completed
    • Custom labels for margin and best-sellers

  4. We submit the feed, work through Google’s review and fix anything still flagged. Where a review is needed, we request it with the fixes in place.

    You get: Products approved and showing.

    • Feed submitted and processed
    • Remaining errors fixed
    • Reviews requested where needed
    • Free listings switched on

  5. We link Google Ads, hand over a feed report and checklist, and check the diagnostics every week for 30 days, so new products and price changes don’t create new errors.

    You get: A healthy feed you know how to keep healthy.

    • Google Ads and GA4 linked
    • A walkthrough call
    • Weekly diagnostics for 30 days
    • A checklist for new products

What we set up

Eight parts of Merchant Center, set up properly

For each part: why it matters, what we set up, what we usually find in existing accounts and what we change.

Area 1 of 8

Account and verification

Before any product can show, Google checks that the store is yours and that it’s a real business, with clear contact details and policies.

What we set up

  • Website verified and claimed
  • Business name, address and phone
  • Contact page and customer service details
  • Refund and return policy pages
  • Secure checkout
  • Users and access

What we often find

  • ! Website never claimed
  • ! No contact details on the site
  • ! Return policy missing or hard to find
  • ! Account owned by a former developer

What we change

  • A verified, claimed website
  • Business details that match the site
  • Policy pages Google can find
  • Admin access in your name

Area 2 of 8

Store connection and feed source

How products get into Merchant Center decides how often they update and how easy they are to fix. The right method depends on your platform and range.

What we set up

  • Shopify Google channel
  • WooCommerce plugin or feed
  • Feed files for other platforms
  • Update schedule
  • Supplemental feeds
  • Feed rules

What we often find

  • ! Two feeds sending the same products
  • ! A feed file updated by hand once a month
  • ! An app that overwrites every fix
  • ! Variants sent as one product

What we change

  • One clean source of products
  • Updates on a schedule that matches the store
  • Fixes in feed rules, so they stay fixed
  • Each variant sent as its own product

Area 3 of 8

Shipping, tax and returns

Shipping costs and delivery times show in your ads and free listings. If they’re missing or wrong, products can’t show in that country, or customers get a surprise at checkout.

What we set up

  • Shipping costs per country
  • Delivery times
  • Free shipping thresholds
  • Tax settings where needed
  • Return policy and window
  • Markets you sell to

What we often find

  • ! No shipping set for a country you sell to
  • ! Delivery times missing
  • ! Free shipping on the site but not in Merchant Center
  • ! Return policy not added

What we change

  • Shipping and delivery times for every market
  • Free shipping thresholds that match the site
  • Returns set, so they show in listings
  • Settings checked against checkout

Area 4 of 8

Titles and descriptions

Titles decide which searches your products show for. Google reads the first words most, so the important details go first.

What we set up

  • Brand, product type and key attributes
  • Order of words by category
  • Best-sellers written by hand
  • Feed rules for the rest
  • Descriptions with materials and use
  • No promotional text

What we often find

  • ! Titles copied from the store, often just a name
  • ! Size and colour missing from titles
  • ! “Free delivery” and “Sale” in titles
  • ! Descriptions empty or copied from suppliers

What we change

  • Titles in the order people search
  • Attributes added from your product data
  • Promotional text removed
  • Descriptions that answer buyers’ questions

Area 5 of 8

Identifiers and attributes

GTINs, brands and model numbers let Google match your products to searches. Some categories also need size, colour, gender, age group or material.

What we set up

  • GTINs from suppliers
  • Brand and MPN
  • Own-brand products marked correctly
  • Google product category
  • Size, colour and gender
  • Product type for your own structure

What we often find

  • ! 640 products without GTINs
  • ! Brand left blank
  • ! Own-brand products sent with fake GTINs
  • ! Clothing without sizes or gender

What we change

  • Identifiers added from supplier data
  • Own-brand products marked correctly
  • Categories and product types set
  • Required attributes for each category

Area 6 of 8

Images

Images are the first thing people see in Shopping. Google rejects images with text, watermarks, borders or placeholders, and blurry ones lose clicks.

What we set up

  • Main image for every product
  • Extra images
  • No text, logos or watermarks
  • Size and quality
  • Image for each variant
  • Lifestyle images where allowed

What we often find

  • ! Promotional text on product images
  • ! Placeholder images for new products
  • ! The same image for every colour
  • ! Images too small to show

What we change

  • Clean main images on a plain background
  • An image for each colour or variant
  • Extra images added
  • New products checked before they go live

Area 7 of 8

Prices, stock and sync

The price and availability in your feed must match your site exactly. Mismatches limit products and, if they keep happening, can lead to a warning or a suspension.

What we set up

  • Price and sale price
  • Sale dates
  • Availability and stock
  • Currency
  • Structured data on product pages
  • Automatic item updates

What we often find

  • ! 112 price mismatches in a week
  • ! Sale prices missing from the feed
  • ! Sold-out products still listed
  • ! No structured data on product pages

What we change

  • Feed updates several times a day
  • Sale prices with start and end dates
  • Stock synced from the store
  • Structured data so Google reads the right price

Area 8 of 8

Free listings, labels and promotions

Once the feed is clean, a few extras help it earn more: free listings, custom labels for bidding and promotions that show in your listings.

What we set up

  • Free listings on
  • Custom labels for margin, season and best-sellers
  • Promotions
  • Product reviews feed
  • Google Ads and GA4 links
  • Local inventory if you have shops

What we often find

  • ! Free listings switched off
  • ! No custom labels, so every product is bid on the same way
  • ! Promotions never set up
  • ! Google Ads not linked

What we change

  • Free listings live from day one
  • Custom labels ready for Shopping and Performance Max
  • Promotions for sales
  • Google Ads and GA4 linked

attrs.title: Why products get disapproved
attrs.lead: The issues we fix most often, what they look like in Merchant Center and how we fix them.

items.title: Missing GTIN or brand
items.problem: Products without identifiers get limited, and Google can’t match them to searches.
items.fix: Identifiers added from supplier data, and own-brand products marked correctly.

items.title: Price or stock mismatch
items.problem: The feed shows a different price or availability from the site, often after a sale starts.
items.fix: Feed synced with the store several times a day, plus structured data on product pages.

items.title: Image problems
items.problem: Images with promotional text, watermarks or placeholders are rejected.
items.fix: Clean product images on a plain background, with one for each variant.

items.title: Shipping not set for a country
items.problem: Products can’t show in a country with no shipping settings, even if you deliver there.
items.fix: Shipping costs and delivery times for every market you sell to.

items.title: Missing policies or contact details
items.problem: No return policy or contact information on the site can get the whole account flagged.
items.fix: Policy and contact pages added and linked, and business details that match the site.

items.question: How do I set up Google Merchant Center?
items.answer: Create an account, verify and claim your website, add business details, shipping and tax, then connect your products through your store’s integration or a feed file.

items.question: Is Google Merchant Center free?
items.answer: Yes. Merchant Center is free, and free listings can show your products at no cost. Shopping ads are paid.

items.question: Why are my products disapproved?
items.answer: Usually missing identifiers, price or stock mismatches, image problems or policy issues such as a missing return policy.

items.question: What if my products don’t have GTINs?
items.answer: Own-brand and handmade products often don’t. They should be marked as having no identifier, with the brand set, rather than given made-up numbers.

items.question: Do you work with Shopify and WooCommerce?
items.answer: Yes, and with other platforms through feed files or apps. We pick the connection that keeps your feed up to date.

items.question: Is this the same as Merchant Center suspension help?
items.answer: No. This is setup and feed work. If your account is already suspended, see our Merchant Center suspension help.
